decisions.reason: As a 2023 plug-in line anchored in the firm's core geospatial integration business, it remains a low-cost complementary option and there is no clear signal yet that abandoning it would create more value than waiting.

This authentication and identity delegation service is still cheap to keep open and relevant to enterprise integration, but after two years its standalone traction is less certain and overlap with adjacent identity offerings raises the withdrawal risk.

The open GIS application development framework fits the firm's platform, standards, and ecosystem strategy, so the option value of continued availability still outweighs the cost of keeping it on the market.

The identity and access service supports the firm's move toward broader enterprise integration and is likely inexpensive to maintain, though its proximity to Product C makes later consolidation a meaningful possibility.
As a 2024 consulting workshop built directly on existing expertise and delivery capabilities, it is a very low-cost market test and it is still too early to close this option.
